Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate peripheral, patchy opacities that are more prominent in the lower lung zones, a radiographic pattern classically associated with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) in patients with asthma and nasal polyposis. Options describing central or apical predominance, absence of opacities, or unilateral limitation do not match the visual findings or the typical presentation of this condition.
